newsitem.title: INDIA: India cabinet to consider SIA plan again.
newsitem.headline: India cabinet to consider SIA plan again.

text.p: The Indian cabinet is likely to reconsider the fate of a proposed joint venture between India's Tata Group and Singapore Airlines later this month, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Sunday.
The news agency said the proposal would be decided when the issue of allowing equity partnerships by foreign airlines under a new aviation policy came up for discussion.
On January 24 India decided to allow foreign investors to take stakes of up to 40 percent in domestic airline companies, but did not allow foreign airlines to buy direct stakes.
The ruling has cast doubt on the future of a $600 million plan by Singapore Airlines and the Tatas to start a domestic airline. The proposal has been opposed by Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim.

PTI quoted Industry Ministry sources as saying no decision had been taken on the specific issue of foreign airlines and that the matter was referred back to the Civil Aviation Ministry for re-consideration.
The SIA proposal is considered a pointer to India's free-market reform programme, which was launched in 1991.

"During discussions (in the cabinet), it was felt that the Civil Aviation Ministry could look at it once again. So, as far as the ministry is concerned, the decision (on foreign airlines) is complete," Ibrahim told Business Standard last week.
Industry Secretary Nilmadhab Mohanty, who later moved to a new assignment last month, had said that the Tata-SIA proposal was scuttled by a domestic airline lobby.
Ibrahim said he was opposed to the SIA proposal because Singapore itself did not allow more than five percent stakes in its domestic airlines.
